desc: Read the input N and M.

Parse the M lines to store constraints per row. Use a dictionary where keys are row indices and values are tuples `(min_black_col, max_white_col - 1)`. Initialize `min_black_col` to 0 and `max_white_col - 1` to N for rows not in input.
Extract all unique row indices from the input and sort them.
Iterate through the sorted rows, maintaining a variable `current_max_U` initialized to N.
For each row, calculate `effective_U = min(row_U, current_max_U)`.
Check if `row_L <= effective_U`. If not, print "No" and exit.
If the loop completes without issues, print "Yes".
Run the provided sample inputs to verify correctness.
If any sample fails, debug the logic.
Once verified, the solution is complete.
